history.dynasty: built by local merchants Ahuka and Manyuka; renovated by King Sansara Chandra
history.summary: Stone Nagara-style temple built in 1204 CE by two local merchants, Ahuka and Manyuka, per inscriptions on its walls; the inscriptions state a Shiva shrine already stood on the spot. Shiva is worshipped as Vaidyanath, 'Lord of Physicians', with healing-power lore attached to the lingam's water. The Ravana-Ganesha legend says Ravana's lingam was set down here forever; Dussehra is therefore traditionally not celebrated at Baijnath (verify). The claim that this is one of the 12 Jyotirlingas is DISPUTED — Parli Vaidyanath (Maharashtra) makes the same claim (verify). Renovated later by King Sansara Chandra.

name: Baijnath Vaidyanath Temple
town_description: Baijnath is a small town in Kangra district, Himachal Pradesh, in the Beas valley on the banks of the Binwa river, about 16 km from Palampur at the foothills of the Dhauladhar range. It grew around the 13th-century Vaidyanath Shiva temple and remains a major Shaivite pilgrimage stop, also serving as a gateway to paragliding at Bir-Billing and the Tibetan monasteries of the valley.
